verification_scope: Official source pages were checked for their published claims and links. No source dataset bytes, protected competition data, or local AOI coverage were downloaded in this review.

sources.title: The Geologic Enhanced Mapping System (GEMS) Prize Challenge — Problem Description
verified_claims: The prediction target is geological faults indicative of geothermal resources; the known public fault data are incomplete and may contain inaccuracies.
Experts created an initial private set of new faults and later review may expand labels for final-round rescoring.
The metric uses a triangular distance kernel with 300 m support, alpha 0.2 and beta 0.8.
The submission must be one-band float32 GeoTIFF on the EPSG:32611 100 m grid, with values in [0,1] and null/NaN outside the competition bounds.
sources.limits: This page does not validate any GEMSDOE91 file, score, receipt, account state, or eligibility.

sources.title: GeoDAWN: Airborne magnetic and radiometric surveys of the northwestern Great Basin, Nevada and California
verified_claims: USGS and DOE describe GeoDAWN airborne magnetic and radiometric data as supporting geologic/geophysical mapping and geothermal and critical-mineral studies in the Walker Lane and western Great Basin.
The page describes magnetic information about subsurface structure/geology, radiometric information about surface geology/soil, and coordinated airborne lidar over a similar extent.
The release is marked CC0 1.0 Universal on the USGS page.
sources.limits: This describes the source and its broad purpose; the release files, feature-band correspondence, spatial masks, and exact local coverage were not downloaded or rechecked here.

sources.title: Geologic Map Schema (GeMS) version of the State Geologic Map Compilation (SGMC) Geodatabase of the Conterminous United States
verified_claims: The 2026 release provides a GeMS version of the SGMC and is marked CC0 1.0 Universal.
The compilation combines state geologic maps with scales varying from 1:50,000 to 1:1,000,000.
The USGS warns that map units remain unreconciled across state boundaries and only bedrock maps are represented in states that also have surficial maps.
sources.limits: Not downloaded or clipped to the competition footprint. Scale heterogeneity and map-unit inconsistency make this a cautious context/stratification layer, not ground truth or a uniformly detailed fault map.

sources.title: About 3DEP Products & Services
verified_claims: USGS says The National Map 3DEP products include lidar point clouds and digital elevation models at various horizontal resolutions.
USGS says 3DEP products are available free of charge and without use restrictions.
The page links a lidar-availability application and a 1-meter DEM availability application.
sources.limits: This is a product-level availability/rights statement. It does not prove that 1 m data cover the GeoDAWN footprint, identify suitable tile dates/quality, or validate any bytes; no local coverage query or download was performed.

sources.title: Structural discontinuities and their control on hydrothermal systems in the Great Basin, USA
sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey Publications Warehouse record for a peer-reviewed article
verified_claims: The abstract describes fault interactions/intersections and eight structural-discontinuity settings as controls on many Great Basin hydrothermal systems.
The reported stress/strain modelling emphasizes fault stepovers and terminations among settings with concentrated effects.
sources.limits: Regional process evidence does not establish that a particular pixel or lineament is a geothermal fault, and it is not a leaderboard-performance result.

sources.title: Slip tendency and dilation tendency of Quaternary faults in the Great Basin region
sources.organization: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Report 2026-5073
verified_claims: The report describes slip/dilation tendency calculated for Quaternary fault segments from the USGS Quaternary Fault and Fold Database.
The abstract says high slip/dilation tendencies in high-strain-rate areas are potentially more prospective for hydrothermal permeability and fluid flow.
sources.limits: Because the calculations are attached to mapped Quaternary fault segments, directly rasterizing their geometry/values risks reproducing the existing-fault catalogue and contaminating a fault holdout. Use only after label-blind leakage review; preferably as a mechanism/control study, not direct evidence of new faults.
